lens.title: Neighbours and Clues
lens.selectPrompt: Tap every tile that touches the outlined one.
lens.countPrompt: How many tiles touching the outlined one are the same colour as it?
lens.complementPrompt: This clue touches {n} tiles and says {count} are {named}. How many are {other}?
lens.stmtCorrect: {count} of the {n} tiles touching it are {colour}.
lens.stmtColor: {count} of the tiles touching it are {colour}.
lens.stmtDiagonal: {count} tiles beside it, not counting corners, are {colour}.
lens.printSelect: Circle every tile that touches the outlined one ({where}). ____
lens.printCount: How many tiles touching the outlined one ({where}) are the same colour as it? ____
lens.printComplement: {where}. It touches {n} tiles and {count} of them are {named}. How many are {other}? ____
lens.method1: A tile touches the tiles beside it, above it, below it, and the four corners.
lens.method2: At an edge or a corner, only the tiles inside the board count.
lens.method3: A clue never counts its own tile.
lens.hintStart: Start with the tiles directly above, below, left and right.
lens.hintHave: You have {count} of them. The corner-touching tiles count too.
lens.hintTouches: An outlined tile {where} touches {n} tiles — the ones off the board do not exist.
lens.hintCount1: Look at the outlined tile's own colour first. Then check each tile around it.
lens.hintCount2: Each tile counts once, and the outlined one is left out.
lens.hintRead1: A clue has two parts: which colour it counts, and how many.
lens.hintRead2: It counts the {n} tiles it touches. Not itself, and all four corners count.
lens.hintComp2: Some of those {n} are {colour}. There are only two colours, so the rest are the other one.
lens.selfNudge: That is the outlined tile itself. A tile never touches itself.
lens.selfSay: That is the tile we are asking about.
lens.chooseFirst: Choose the tiles that touch the outlined one first.
lens.setRightMsg: All {n} tiles that touch it, and nothing else.
lens.setWrongMsg: It touches {n} tiles — the four beside it and the four corners, minus any off the board.
lens.countMsgComp: {n} tiles touch it and {count} are {named}, so {answer} are {other}.
lens.countMsg: {answer} of the {n} tiles touching it match.
lens.stmtRightMsg: The colour it counts, and how many of the tiles it touches.
lens.trapSelf: A clue never counts its own tile.
lens.trapColor: Check which colour the clue is counting.

board.title: Colour the Board
board.partialPrompt: Colour only the tiles these clues can settle, and leave the rest blank. Use {names}.
board.fullPrompt: Colour every blank tile so all the clues are true. Use {names}.
board.printed: Colour every blank tile so all the clues are true. Each clue counts the tiles it touches, including corners, and never itself. ____
board.method1: Read each clue: which colour it counts, and how many.
board.method2: A clue that has all its matches already leaves nothing else that colour.
board.method3: A clue that needs as many as there are spaces left fills every one of them.
board.stepZero: It allows no {colour} neighbours at all, so every blank tile it touches is the other colour.
board.stepFull: It needs every touching tile to be {colour}. Start at {first}.
board.stepExclude: It already has {count} {colour} tiles. {first} must be another colour.
board.stepFill: It needs {remaining} more {colour}, exactly the open choices left. Start at {first}.
board.stepOverExclude: Shared tiles already use the {colour} count. {first} cannot be {colour}.
board.stepOverFill: Comparing the clues leaves {colour} for {first}. Colour that tile next.
board.hintDone: Every clue that can still say something has said it. Check what you have.
board.hintReread: Read each clue again and count the tiles it touches.

missing.one: {count} tile the clues do settle is still blank.
missing.other: {count} tiles the clues do settle are still blank.

board.partialGuess: One of those was a guess
board.partialRightMsg: And you left the rest blank, because these clues cannot decide them yet.
board.partialGuessMsg: These two clues cannot decide every tile. Where they cannot, the answer is to leave it blank and look for another clue.
board.partialWrongMsg: Compare what the two clues share against what only one of them touches.
board.unsolvedTitle: One clue is not true yet
board.solvedMsg: Each tile has a reason, and all the clues agree.
board.recountAround: Count around {name} and compare it with what it says.
board.recount: Recount {name} and compare it with what it says.
board.checkEach: Check each clue against the tiles it touches.

lab.title: Give a Reason
lab.comparePrompt: Which clues are enough, on their own, to decide the outlined tile?
lab.choosePrompt: The outlined tile has been worked out. Which of these says why?
lab.findPrompt: Somebody coloured this board and one tile is wrong. Tap a clue that is not true.
lab.printFind: One tile in this board is the wrong colour. Write down a clue that is not true, and why. ____
lab.printCompare: Which clues are enough on their own to decide the outlined tile{spot}? ____
lab.printWhy: Write down why the outlined tile{spot} must be the colour it is. ____
lab.method1: A set of clues is enough when it decides the tile without any other help.
lab.method2: A reason names the clue, the colour it counts, and what that leaves.
lab.method3: To check a board, count each clue's colour around it and compare with its number.
lab.hintCompare1: Take one option at a time and ask: with only these clues, could I still work the tile out?
lab.hintCompare2: A clue that is true but says nothing about this tile is not evidence for it.
lab.hintChoose1: A reason has to name a clue, and say what that clue leaves for this tile.
lab.hintChoose2: More than one reason may work. Reject any that misread what a clue counts.
lab.hintFind1: Take one clue and count its colour around it. Compare that with its number.
lab.hintFind2: Work through the clues in turn. The wrong tile may break more than one.
lab.enoughMsg: With only those clues the tile still comes out.
lab.fairMsg: It names a clue and says what that clue leaves.
lab.trapNotEnough: That clue is true, but on its own it leaves the tile open.
lab.trapUnrelated: That clue says nothing about this tile.
lab.trapSelf: A clue never counts its own tile.
lab.trapColor: Check which colour the clue counts, and where.
lab.noClueNudge: That tile has no clue on it. Tap one with a number.
lab.brokenMsg: Count its colour around it and compare with its number — they do not match.
lab.holdsMsg: Count around it: it says {count}, and that is what is there. Try another.

why.zeroA: {name} allows no {colour} at all, so this tile cannot be {colour}.
why.zeroB: Nothing {name} touches is {colour}, and this tile touches it.
why.fullA: {name} needs every tile it touches, so this one is {colour}.
why.fullB: There are exactly as many tiles as {name} needs, so none of them can be {other}.
why.exclA: {name} already has all the {colour} it needs, so this tile is not {colour}.
why.exclB: Counting the {colour} already around {name} reaches its number, leaving none for this tile.
why.fillA: {name} still needs more {colour}, and this is one of the only tiles left for it.
why.fillB: Take the {colour} already found away from {name}, and what is missing exactly fills the spaces left.
why.overExclA: Comparing {name} with the other clue over the same tiles accounts for all its {colour}, so this tile has none left.
why.overExclB: The tiles the two clues share already carry every {colour} {name} allows.
why.overFillA: Comparing {name} with the other clue leaves this tile as the one that must be {colour}.
why.overFillB: Subtracting the smaller clue from the larger one leaves {colour} with nowhere else to go.
why.runA: Every arrangement {name} still allows puts {colour} here.
why.runB: Ruling out the arrangements {name} forbids leaves only ones where this tile is {colour}.
why.wSelf: {name} counts itself as well, and that is what settles this tile.
why.wColor: {name} is about how many tiles are {colour} somewhere on the board.
why.wDiag: {name} counts only the tiles beside it, not the corners.
why.wNear: {name} counts the tiles nearest to it.
